facts.fact: The final evaluation for Enabel (COTA, fieldwork April 2026) says the transfer of E-RENEC's source code to the Guinean side is formal but not operational, national technicians have no access to it, and the system is vulnerable and dependent on outside expertise, with no multi-year maintenance plan or central support service.

The evaluation says E-RENEC was developed under PARECIGUI Phase 2, implemented by Enabel under a financing agreement from April 2024 to February 2026, and that at its close there was no dedicated maintenance budget and no operating budget secured; sustainability is rated C.

The evaluation says the exclusion in July 2025 of the health, security and religious affairs ministries, the entry points for declarations of births, marriages and deaths, directly compromised E-RENEC's declarations module (module 3), which was not developed, and left interoperability non-existent.

The evaluation says that when Enabel's project ended in February 2026 interoperability between E-RENEC and PN-RAVEC had not been activated, for want of a political decision, registrars in the field still used paper in parallel, and consulates did not use the equipment delivered and produced no digital acts.

note: No events, made or offices fact: the summary names no event entered digitally (the declarations module was not built), does not say where or when a record is entered, and gives no count of offices; the evaluators were refused access to civil status centres.
